summary:
Objective: Maximize Factorio’s PvP production score at 0:20:00. Current time 0:05:39, score 716. Hand and machine production both count; inputs and fuel used are deducted, science spent on research retains its value. Ore/coal are about 3 points each and plates about 6. Rock-mined stone did not directly raise the score, but is useful for furnaces. Steam power unlocked automatically after producing 50 iron plates. Nothing is currently being researched.

Layout: Spawn is southeast of the main iron patch (initial walk NW about 5 seconds to its east edge). Copper borders iron on the northwest/west side; stone is northeast of iron. Water is farther east/southeast, east or northeast of coal. Coal is southeast of iron, on the northwest edge of a dense forest; approach from the north to avoid trees. From the starter iron setup, walk SE about 8.5 seconds then S about 3 seconds to reach the coal drills; reverse to return. Two burner coal drills stand vertically adjacent and face into each other; both are working and accumulating fuel. Starter iron burner drill on the east side of iron faces north directly into a stone furnace; it is still working as of last check but will need fuel soon. It also has hand-mined ore in its input. No power infrastructure, labs, assemblers, belts or chests built yet.

Current position: southern part of iron, immediately south of a newly placed horizontal row of four unfueled burner iron drills. The four all face north. At the last view, 1280×720, their approximate centers are (528,235), (592,235), (656,235), (720,235). Furnace centers should be one 2-tile footprint (64 px) north, around y=171. The starter pair is far NE of this position, at the upper right edge of the last screen. Several rocks on the SW/south edge of iron have been mined for stone.

Inventory: about 6 stone furnaces, 25 coal, 1 wood, no carried plates or ore, no spare drills. Starter furnace has accumulated some additional plates since the last collection. Main hotbar is empty; pistol and 10 magazines are equipped.

Next: Place four furnaces directly north of the new drills (horizontal drag works), move close enough for interactions, and fuel all four pairs. With only 25 coal, seed each with a few and go collect more; refuel the starter pair too. Harvest coal from the facing drills periodically, leaving some fuel or relying on their ongoing burn to restart the loop. Add another coal pair soon to support expansion. Use the rising plate supply for more iron drill/furnace pairs and at least one copper pair. Steam power is available; consider scaling to electric mining if the recipe unlocks and the distance from water make it worthwhile, otherwise keep scaling burner pairs and fuel supply. Keep output slots from filling; convert surplus plates into useful higher-value crafts toward the deadline. Avoid long idle waits while there’s useful building or mining to do.

Controls: Game time advances during actions, not thinking, and each action costs roughly a second overhead. Briefly say what you’re doing and why, and keep acting until the deadline. WASD movement, diagonals work; at current zoom one tile is 32 px. Short movements can overshoot because of additional action time; check the resulting view. Hold E about 0.25–0.35 s for inventory/crafting; taps sometimes don’t register, and short mouse clicks sometimes only move the pointer. For reliable world placement use a left hold around 0.3 s, or drag to place a row. Inventory opens centered; first item slot (340,240), slots 30 px apart. Production crafting tab (762,220); after steam power, burner drill recipe (668,300), stone furnace (668,330). Right-click recipe crafts up to five; use a held right click if ordinary click misses. Burner drill costs 9 iron plates and 1 stone furnace. To place, pick up the item in inventory and close with E; Q clears cursor. R rotates 90°, twice reverses; look for the yellow output arrow. The last four drills were placed facing north; verify orientation on new batches. Ctrl+left with an empty cursor takes machine output, Ctrl+left with a held stack inserts it, Ctrl+right inserts half the held stack (use held clicks if needed). Right-hold to mine ore (~1 per 2 seconds) or nearby rocks (~5 seconds for 20 stone); red selection often means out of reach, so move closer rather than waiting. M opens/closes map; T opens technology. The console and editor are disabled; never quit to the main menu.

No other players or agreements. Enemies are peaceful unless attacked; leave them alone.

summary:
Objective: Maximize Factorio’s PvP production score at game time 0:20:00. At 0:08:00 the score was 1,686. Hand and machine output both count; consumed ingredients and fuel are deducted. Ore, stone, and coal are about 3 points each, plates about 6, and crafted goods generally add value. Science packs retain their value when used in labs. Wood and fish are worth nothing, and stone mined from rocks is useful for crafting but did not itself raise the score.

Built and running: Five burner iron drill/furnace pairs. Four form a contiguous east–west row in the south of the iron patch, with drills feeding furnaces directly to the north. The original pair is farther northeast on the east side of iron. All were running recently. The original pair and four main drills were refueled around 7:06–7:19, but the middle two furnaces in the four-wide row received little or no extra fuel and will need attention first. The row’s plates were collected at 7:24–7:26. Four coal drills form a 2×2 block, arranged as two independent north–south pairs facing into one another. Both are running; the original east pair was harvested at 6:32 and the new west pair started at 6:45. No power, labs, assemblers, belts, or storage chests built yet.

Research: Steam power unlocked automatically after 50 iron plates. Nothing is being researched. Producing 10 copper plates unlocks Electronics (circuits, labs, small poles, etc.); crafting one lab unlocks red science. Electric mining drills then take 25 red packs at 10 seconds per pack in one lab. Parallel labs would speed that up if worthwhile.

Layout: Spawn is southeast of the main iron patch; the original iron pair is roughly 5 seconds NW of spawn. Copper borders iron to the west/northwest. Stone is northeast/east of iron, near trees. Coal is southeast of iron on the northwest edge of a dense forest. From just south of the original iron pair, walk SE (S+D) for about 8.5 seconds and then due S for 2.5 seconds to arrive alongside the coal drills; reverse to return. This avoids the forest. Water is east/northeast of coal, farther east/southeast of iron. No other players. Enemies are peaceful unless attacked.

Current position and inventory: Standing by the remains of a large mined rock northeast of iron, with the stone patch visible at the right edge and iron/copper down-left. From the western end of the four-wide iron row, I walked S for 0.63 s, NE for 4.35 s, then N for 0.8 s to get here. Inventory is open on the Production tab. Slots from left at y=240: wood 1, coal 29, stone 21, iron ore 2, iron plates 29. Five burner drills just queued, including intermediate gears and furnaces; they’ll finish while moving. No spare furnaces yet. Hotbar empty; pistol and 10 magazines equipped. View is zoomed out three notches from the earlier 32 px/tile view.

Next steps:
1. While inventory is open, craft four stone furnaces from the 21 stone. Consider a stone drill into an iron chest so stone accumulates without further hand mining; bring more fuel and craft additional drills as iron comes in.
2. Return southwest/west to the copper–iron border and place at least two burner copper pairs, with adjacent furnaces directly in the output direction. The last burner drill cursor orientation was south; rotate twice to north if using the same layout as iron. Give the pairs enough fuel, then use the remaining drills for more iron or coal. The existing iron row can be extended or duplicated.
3. Collect coal again and top up machines. Four coal drills produce close to one coal/sec before fuel deduction, so expand with more facing pairs as needed. A full stack lasts a long time in a burner; prioritize avoiding frequent tiny refuels. Watch for coal drills filling their fuel slots and stalling; harvest both sides of each pair together.
4. After 10 copper plates, build a lab and consider steam power at the nearby water (offshore pump, boiler, steam engine, and small poles). Keep burner production growing while red science crafts/research runs. Electric drills into chests can cheaply scale raw production if the grid and research are ready with enough time left; don’t let a long power project stall the existing production. Collect outputs before slots fill, and craft higher-value goods with surplus plates near the deadline.

Controls learned: WASD, diagonals work; short movements can go farther than expected. E held about 0.25 s reliably opens/closes inventory, T similarly opens/closes tech, M opens map. Inventory slots start at (341,240), advance 30 px. Production tab is (762,220); at current unlocks burner drill recipe is (668,300) and stone furnace (668,330). Hold right mouse ~0.2 s on a recipe to craft up to five. Burner drill costs 9 iron plates plus one stone furnace (5 stone if auto-crafted). Pick up a stack with left click, close inventory with E, place in world with left hold ~0.25 s or drag to place a row. Q clears cursor, or pipettes a hovered entity when empty. Hold R ~0.2 s for one quarter-turn; twice reverses. Check output arrows/linked entity highlights. Ordinary taps can miss; held actions are more reliable.

Ctrl+left with empty cursor takes output (including coal from coal drill fuel inventory); Ctrl+left with a held stack inserts it; Ctrl+right inserts half. Use ~0.2 s held mouse clicks. Ctrl+left drag can collect a row but sometimes skips alternate machines; drag back or click individually. With coal held, hovering a burner and holding Z for about 0.4 s inserts about 3 coal, 0.9 s about 6. Be careful using Ctrl+right immediately after another machine: a held transfer can also hit the previous machine if pointer movement lags, so check the floating quantities. Right-hold mine ore or actual rocks; small scattered rock textures often aren’t mineable. Red brackets can mean out of reach. Large rocks are worth mining for stone; the last yielded 46 stone total by the time inventory was opened. Game time advances during actions, with roughly a second overhead per action; briefly state what you’re doing, and continue until 20:00. Never use console/editor or quit to main menu.

No player messages or agreements. Unresolved: exact shoreline access, whether electric mining will repay its setup time, and current fuel levels in the middle furnaces.

summary:

Production counts whether mined or crafted by hand or machine, and whether collected or left in output. Raw resources are worth roughly 3 each and plates roughly 6; ingredients and fuel consumed are deducted. Crafting adds value, and science packs retain their value if spent on research. Wood and fish are worthless for score; stone from rocks is useful for construction but did not directly raise the score.

Built: Five burner iron drill/furnace pairs, three burner copper drill/furnace pairs, eight coal drills in four self-feeding pairs, and three burner stone drills feeding three iron chests. No power, labs, assemblers, belts, or inserters. Steam Power and Electronics are unlocked; nothing is researching. We chose to expand burners rather than spend the remaining time on steam and the 25-red-pack Electric Mining Drill research.

Layout: Spawn is southeast of the main iron patch. The original iron pair is on the east edge of iron, about 5 seconds NW of spawn. The other four iron pairs are a contiguous E–W row on the south of the patch. Copper lies W/NW of iron; the three copper pairs are an E–W row. All ore drills point north into directly adjacent furnaces; north-facing burner drills output on the left of their two columns. Stone is east of copper and NE of iron by the forest: from the large rock that was mined north of the copper row, walking due east 5.1 seconds took us to the west edge of stone. The three stone drills are side by side near that west edge, chests immediately north. There are other mineable rocks around the ore patches. Coal is SE of iron, on the NW edge of dense forest. The original three coal pairs form two adjacent E–W rows facing inward, and the new fourth pair is directly south of the west pair. From immediately west of the three coal pairs, walking NW 8.7 seconds, north 1.79 seconds, then NW 0.63 seconds reached the south iron row. From there NW 1.62 seconds reached the east side of copper. Reverse these legs for coal. From stone to coal, south 9.5 sec, SE 1.13 sec, east 2.13 sec also worked. Water is east/NE of coal and east/SE of iron; shoreline not scouted.

Current position: Just east of copper, coal held, pointer already correctly hovering the middle copper drill at (536,370), which has only 3 coal left in its slot. Copper drills x=489,536,583 at y=370, furnaces directly above at y=321. Aim to give drills enough to last much of the remaining run (one coal is about 27 seconds of continuous burner drill operation; a furnace fed by one drill uses much less).

Drag-place a contiguous row of north-facing drills then place furnaces directly on the yellow arrows. Fuels and collections can be done row by row. More coal pairs also pay off and supply the other drills. Harvest the coal pairs about every 2–3 minutes or before their 50-slot fuel limit stalls production. 4. Keep active lines running, collect furnace outputs before they fill, and use spare crafting time/materials to increase score. With little time left queue score-positive crafting with surplus plates rather than starting a power project, and continue acting until the deadline.

Controls and UI: Game clock advances on actions, not while thinking. E held ~0.24 sec reliably opens/closes inventory, T tech, M map. Ctrl+left drag collects a row quickly but occasionally skips its final machine; check or sweep back. Never use console/editor or quit to main menu. Briefly say what you’re doing and why as you play.
